title: The Silent House
description: Assess the 'Acoustics' of your living space. Discover if your home is a sanctuary or a cell.

questions.text: When I return to an empty home, my first feeling is...

options.text: Relief and peace.
Standard routine.
A heavy weight in the chest.
A physical punch of loneliness; I want to leave immediately.

questions.text: I leave the TV or Podcast playing 24/7 just to have 'Background Noise'...

options.text: Never.
Occasionally.
Always; I can't handle the silence.
I feel like I'm dying without a human voice playing.

questions.text: The idea of eating 'Dinner Alone' at a table feels...

options.text: Fine; I enjoy my own company.
A bit sad.
Pathetic; I eat on the couch or bed instead.
Agonizing; I often skip meals to avoid the feeling.

insight_cloud.title: Touch Hunger
insight_cloud.text: Living in a 'Silent House' often leads to 'Skin Hunger' or 'Touch Starvation'—a physical deficiency in skin-to-skin contact. Since your brain needs this for brain health, the 'House' starts to feel like a 'Void'. Using weighted blankets or pets can provide a temporary biological bridge.

options.text: Representative of me.
A bit random.
Like a museum of a person I used to be.
Like a warehouse; there is no 'me' here.

questions.text: Do you feel like your 'house' is slowly eating your personality?

options.text: No.
Sometimes.
Frequently.
Yes, I am being absorbed by the drywall.
